screening_decisions.reason: Randomised controlled trial evaluating transfer of breast cancer follow-up from hospital to general practice, which is a continuity-of-care intervention. Population is women with breast cancer in remission. Outcomes include time to recurrence diagnosis and validated quality-of-life scales (SF-36, EORTC, HADS).
This is a systematic review of guideline dissemination strategies across general conditions, not a primary RCT, CCT, CBA, or ITS. It does not focus on cancer continuity interventions.

Randomised controlled trial comparing nurse-led versus conventional medical follow-up for lung cancer patients. Directly evaluates a continuity intervention in cancer follow-up with patient and process outcomes.
Study population is terminally ill patients in general; the abstract does not specify that >50% have cancer, nor is the intervention explicitly designed to improve continuity of cancer care.
Review article examining determinants of place of death. Not an intervention evaluation of eligible design.
Epidemiological modeling and projection study. Not an intervention evaluation.

Randomized controlled trial of a pivot nurse in oncology for lung or breast cancer patients. The nurse role is intended to improve continuity of care. Uses validated patient-reported outcome measures.
Population is patients with type 2 diabetes, not cancer. Study aims to develop a measurement instrument rather than evaluate an intervention to improve continuity.

Although randomized and in cancer patients, the intervention is a pain education programme targeting pain knowledge and analgesic use, not continuity of care or coordination between providers/settings.

Randomized controlled trial evaluating tailored information faxed to GPs about chemotherapy patients. This is a shared-care/continuity intervention targeting healthcare providers of adults with cancer. Outcomes include provider confidence, knowledge, and satisfaction.
Cochrane systematic review of shared care for chronic diseases in general. Not a primary study of eligible design and not specific to cancer continuity.

Randomized clinical trial of advanced practice nurse interventions during initial treatment. The intervention is supportive care during the acute treatment phase, not an intervention specifically designed to improve continuity of care in follow-up.

Randomized study of intensified primary care for newly diagnosed cancer patients, explicitly designed to increase information from specialist care to primary care and improve continuity. Outcomes include follow-up contacts and continuing contact rates.

Very brief abstract indicates a patient-held QOL diary. The intervention concerns QOL self-monitoring, not continuity of care. Study design details are insufficient and it does not appear to be an eligible controlled design.
Systematic review of educational interventions. Not a primary study of eligible design.
Randomized study of post-surgical nursing support. The intervention targets physical and psychological recovery after surgery, not continuity of care or coordination across providers/settings.

Randomised controlled trial explicitly evaluating coordination of care for terminally ill cancer patients via nurse coordinators. Directly tests a continuity/coordination intervention with patient, carer, and service outcomes.
Quasi-experimental design with surveys comparing telenursing to traditional home health for ostomy patients. Quasi-experimental studies are not among the eligible designs (RCT, CCT, CBA, ITS).
Randomised trial of early hospital discharge after breast cancer surgery. The intervention concerns length of acute postoperative stay, not continuity of care in the follow-up setting.
Review/methods paper exploring illness trajectories. Not an intervention evaluation of eligible design.
Conceptual review of continuity and related concepts. Not an intervention study.
Review/article articulating models of survivorship care. Not an intervention evaluation of eligible design.
Randomized controlled trial evaluating algorithmic cancer pain management guidelines. The intervention targets pain management, not continuity of care or coordination between providers.
Review paper on patient-physician communication. Not an intervention study of eligible design.
Systematic review of antibiotic prescribing for acute outpatient infections. Wrong population and not an eligible primary study design.
Review paper. Not a primary intervention evaluation.

Prospective randomised study of patients on a gynaecological oncology ward, evaluating an intervention to increase GP-hospital contact and provide discharge summaries. Explicitly framed as continuity of care with satisfaction and confidence outcomes.
Instrument validation study (PCCQ) in general inpatients. Not an evaluation of an intervention to improve continuity, and population is not focused on cancer.

This abstract is a commentary or editorial discussing the trial by Grunfeld et al., not the primary trial report itself. It cites other studies and provides opinion rather than presenting primary trial data.

Randomised controlled trial of a hospital palliative care team for inpatients with cancer and other chronic diseases. The abstract does not confirm that >50% of participants had cancer, and the intervention is a palliative care service model rather than specifically a continuity intervention.
Literature review of nurse-led follow-up and telephone interventions. Not a primary study of eligible design.
Conceptual review and terminology clarification article. Not an intervention evaluation.
The provided abstract is about ATP biosensors in Escherichia coli, which is completely mismatched and irrelevant to cancer continuity. Exclude.

Subset analysis from a factorial trial of geriatric evaluation units for hospitalized frail elderly patients. The intervention is geriatric assessment and management, not specifically designed to improve continuity of cancer care.

Feasibility trial with trial arms evaluating a complex intervention explicitly designed to improve experienced continuity of care in cancer patients. Uses a patient-completed continuity assessment with feedback to clinicians. Controlled design with patient outcomes.
Observational study using Medicare claims to compare care received by cancer survivors versus controls. Not an intervention evaluation.
Epidemiological surveillance report. Not an intervention study.

Randomised controlled trial of nurse-led early discharge after breast cancer surgery. The intervention concerns acute postoperative hospital length of stay, not continuity of care in cancer follow-up.
Literature review of continuity of care research methods. Not a primary intervention evaluation.

Randomized clinical trial of a computer-based nursing intervention for psychological support of newly diagnosed patients during chemotherapy. The primary focus is psychosocial support, not continuity of care or coordination.
Instrument development study in diabetes patients. Wrong population and not an intervention evaluation.
Observational study using SEER-Medicare data. Not an intervention evaluation of eligible design.
Review/discussion paper describing challenges in continuity for advanced cancer patients in Canada. Not an intervention evaluation.

Randomized controlled trial of a Pain Education Programme. Although the abstract mentions continuity of care in the context of district nurses, the intervention itself is pain education for patients and nurses, not a care coordination or continuity intervention.

Quasi-experimental study comparing a transmural home care intervention (explicitly intending to optimize cooperation and coordination between hospital and community) versus standard care for terminal cancer patients. Meets eligible controlled design (CCT/CBA) and targets continuity.

Randomized trial of a nurse-driven, computer-assisted supportive intervention for prostate cancer patients after treatment. Focuses on quality-of-life education and support, not continuity or care coordination.
Literature review of continuity of care concepts. Not a primary intervention study.

Randomised controlled trial evaluating case conferences between GPs and specialist palliative care teams as a coordination/continuity intervention. Palliative care populations are typically majority cancer patients; abstract describes specialist palliative care services where cancer is the predominant diagnosis.
Qualitative case study using semi-structured interviews to describe coordination mechanisms. Not an RCT, CCT, CBA, or ITS.
Review and commentary on survivorship care plans. Not a primary intervention evaluation.
Meta-analysis of follow-up strategies. Not a primary study of eligible design.
Qualitative study using focus groups and interviews. Not an eligible quantitative controlled design.
Randomized clinical trial of a daily pain management diary for outpatients with cancer-related pain. The intervention concerns pain self-management and diary use, not continuity of care.

Evaluation of an Extended Information Routine from specialist clinic to GP for cancer patients, with patients randomized to extended versus standard information. Assesses GP knowledge and support as outcomes. This is an informational continuity intervention targeting healthcare providers of adults with cancer.
Scoping exercise and overview of literature. Not a primary intervention study.

Controlled evaluation comparing women with breast cancer receiving information cards for their GP versus a non-intervention group. The cards aim to improve communication between hospital and primary care, which is an informational continuity intervention.
Survey-based taxonomy development of shared care models for chronic disease in general. Not specific to cancer and not an intervention evaluation.

Study allocating cancer patients to routine psychosocial assessment with real-time feedback to oncologists versus control. The intervention is patient-reported outcome feedback, not a continuity or care-coordination intervention.
Cochrane review of computer reminder systems. Not a primary study and not specific to cancer continuity.
Qualitative descriptive study of implementing a patient-navigator role. Not an RCT, CCT, CBA, or ITS.
Cross-sectional population-based survey comparing cancer survivors to controls. Not an intervention evaluation.
Cross-sectional analysis of National Health Interview Survey data. Not an intervention study.
Self-administered survey of patients' perspectives on follow-up care. Not an intervention evaluation of eligible design.

Pragmatic randomised controlled trial evaluating patient-held records for continuing care of cancer patients. Explicitly targets continuity and communication across care levels. Outcomes include quality of life, patient/professional views, and resource use.
Instrument validation study (CCAENA). Not an evaluation of an intervention to improve continuity.
Randomised study of psychological support from breast care nurses around the time of surgery. The intervention targets acute psychological morbidity, not continuity of care in follow-up.

Randomised controlled trial with waiting list evaluating a palliative care home support team. The abstract does not specify cancer as the majority diagnosis, and the study focuses on service evaluation rather than continuity mechanisms.
Qualitative research study. Not an eligible quantitative controlled design.
Survey study of primary care physician satisfaction and communication with radiation oncologists. Not an intervention evaluation of eligible design.

Randomised controlled trial of a supplementary patient-held record for radiotherapy outpatients. Directly evaluates a tool intended to improve communication, participation, and continuity across providers.
Randomized trial comparing family physician versus specialist long-term follow-up for early-stage breast cancer. Directly tests a continuity of care model in cancer follow-up.

Randomised, unblinded clinical trial evaluating a structured oncology information pack sent to GPs of newly referred cancer patients. Targets informational continuity between specialist and primary care with provider outcomes.
Systematic review of hypertension quality improvement. Wrong population and not a primary study.
Guidance article on taking a survivor-directed medical history. Not an intervention evaluation.
Randomized controlled trial of pain assessment feedback to oncologists. The intervention targets pain management, not continuity of care.

Cluster-randomized demonstration project of home health agency interventions (oncology nurse specialist and education). The intervention targets home health quality, not explicitly continuity or coordination of cancer follow-up.
Analysis of quality-of-life data from treatment trials to examine depression prevalence. Not an intervention evaluation for continuity.

Randomized clinical trial comparing oncology home care, standard home care, and office care for progressive lung cancer. The intervention concerns home nursing support rather than continuity or care coordination mechanisms.
Randomized trial of coordinated psychosocial interventions based on patient self-assessments. The coordination refers to psychosocial care, not continuity of medical follow-up or care transitions.
Cohort study using propensity score methods comparing long-term cancer survivors to controls. Not an intervention evaluation.

Cluster randomized trial of a palliative care intervention based on cooperation between a palliative medicine unit and community services versus conventional care. Explicitly integrates hospital and community care for malignant disease patients, representing a cross-boundary continuity intervention.

Randomised controlled trial comparing general practice versus surgical-based follow-up for colon cancer patients. Directly evaluates a continuity/follow-up model with quality of life, anxiety, depression, and satisfaction outcomes.
Systematic review of patient-held records in cancer care. Not a primary study of eligible design.
Instrument development study in cardiac patients. Wrong population and not an intervention evaluation.

Randomized prospective trial of nurse case management for 12 months after breast cancer diagnosis in older women. Case management is a coordination/continuity intervention. Outcomes include treatment use and patient satisfaction.
Working group report and commentary on comorbidity assessment. Not an intervention evaluation.

Randomized controlled trial of a single telephone follow-up call 48-72 hours after hospital discharge. This is a brief post-discharge contact, not a continuity of care intervention in the follow-up setting.
Observational study using SEER-Medicare claims to examine mammography use by follow-up model. Not a randomized or controlled intervention evaluation.
Survey of nurses and physicians about internal communication and transfer to palliative care. Not an intervention evaluation of eligible design.
Randomized controlled trial of routine HRQL measurement and feedback in oncology practice. The intervention is patient-reported outcome use, not a continuity or care-coordination intervention.
Conceptual and definitional article. Not an intervention evaluation and not specific to cancer.
Descriptive and qualitative study of the number of doctors encountered by cancer patients and patient perspectives. Not an intervention evaluation of eligible design.
